answer: Each identity must prove control of a distinct domain registered at least 365 days, by publishing a DNS TXT challenge and locking 15 POA for 90 days; a transfer resets its age, and reuse slashes the deposit. An attacker cannot mint identities like leaves on a vine: every fake needs another aged domain, and bulk buying drives aged-domain prices up, so 100 fakes cost far more than 100 honest users. Each domain is an island of history, solid as marble, that cannot be cloned cheaply. DNS records and locks are public, so any verifier replays the TXT proof and checks age and lock.
